title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics (v26)
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce wasted padding in continuous/dynamic batching by grouping requests into sequence-length buckets and applying lightweight packing heuristics, and make small scheduler/kernel changes to improve throughput for mixed-length workloads. This changeset implements a production-tuned seqlen bucketing strategy with configurable bucket boundaries, a padding-minimization packing pass, and a scheduler hint API so the runtime can prefer kernels that are optimal for each bucket. Key points: 1) Bucketing: introduced a new SeqlenBucketManager that computes bucket boundaries from observed request seqlen distribution (percentile-based) and exposes a mutable bucket config. Buckets are chosen to minimize expected padding cost given recent traffic. 2) Packing/minimization: added an in-batcher packing step which reorders and packs multiple short requests into a shared slot where the model supports prefix-kv concatenation; includes safety checks for KV cache correctness and per-customer isolation. 3) Scheduler hints and kernel selection: added lightweight metadata on batched work items so the worker can select optimized attention kernels and reduce cross-bucket padding copies. 4) KV cache improvements: amortized KV cache lookups for packed prefixes and added a fast-path for no-op cache hits to avoid unnecessary synchronization. 5) Telemetry and tuning: added new metrics (seqlen_bucket.{id}.padding_waste, bucket_fill_ratio, pack_reject_rate) and a runtime flag to enable/disable packing per deployment. Benchmarks: internal perf lab (A100, seq mix from production trace) shows median token latency improved by ~6% and overall token throughput improved by ~11% at 95th percentile load; worst-case P95 latency for mixed short+long traffic reduced by ~18% compared to current master. Safety/regression: added unit tests for bucket boundary computation, integration tests to validate KV cache invariants with packing, and a staged rollout plan to enable packing as an opt-in flag. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior (packing disabled) until the runtime flag is enabled. Related work: builds on prior dynamic-batching efforts in prs: pr-99500..pr-104679 family and references ENG-4821. rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag and configurable bucket_sizing policy; recommend enabling on Dedicated first.
commits: 4 commits: 1) seqlen-bucket-manager: initial percentile-based boundary computation and config API; 2) in-batcher-packing: packing pass with KV cache safety checks; 3) scheduler-hints-and-kernel-route: add hint propagation and kernel selection logic; 4) metrics-and-tests: telemetry, unit/integration tests, docs and upgrade notes
review_comments: Michael Chen: Left a couple of nits around naming and suggested making the percentile config explicit instead of magic constants.
Asha Patel: Addressed nits in commit 3, added unit test for percentile edge cases.
Sofia Alvarez: Question about performance under extreme long-tail (many >2k tokens) traffic. Suggested adding a safety cap on pack size and rejecting packing for requests with large KV footprints.
Asha Patel: Added pack_reject_rate metric and a runtime cap on packable prefix length; added documentation for the cap and rationale.
Ravi Kothari: Approve after CI green; requested a follow-up to audit operator-visible telemetry naming.
CI system: Full integration suite passed on rerun (one flaky test fixed)
release_notes: Performance: dynamic batching seqlen bucketing and optional prefix packing to reduce padding waste; ~11% token throughput improvement on mixed-length workloads and up to 18% P95 latency reduction in worst-case traces. Feature gated; disable packing if you rely on strict per-request scheduling.
